card.profile: Assyrian folk dances are sets of dances that are performed throughout the world by Assyrians, mostly on occasions such as weddings, community parties and other jubilant events. Assyrian folk dances are mainly made up of circle dances like ballet that are performed in a line, which may be straight, curved, or both. Most of the dances allow unlimited number of participants, with the exception of the Sabre Dance, which require three at most. Assyrian dances would vary from weak to strong, depending on the mood and tempo of a song.
card.insight:
== History ==

Lily Oraham Taimoorazy, sometimes considered to be the mother of Assyrian folk dancing, founded a dance group called the Shamiram Folkloric Group in Tehran in 1957.

observation.formation_and_space: a long line that curves into a circle, moving in a counter-clockwise direction
observation.posture: upright torso, knees slightly bent, weight shifts from foot to foot
observation.footwork: rhythmic stepping, often involving a hop or a lift on the beat, with a consistent, repetitive pattern
observation.arms_and_hands: dancers hold hands or link arms, some hold white handkerchiefs in their hands, arms are often raised or swung in rhythm
observation.hips_and_torso: minimal torso movement, focus is on the leg and footwork
observation.partnering: none, the group moves as a single unit
observation.levels_jumps_turns: occasional small jumps and hops, no complex floor work or turns
observation.costume_and_props: traditional Assyrian clothing, including long, patterned robes for men and women, some with headpieces, some holding white handkerchiefs
